result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_in_degree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the in-degree of a node (directed graphs only). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L17302-L17353){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_in_degree(node) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![In-degree of one node](/assets/graphs/get-in-degree.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A five-node directed graph with the queried node C outlined. The three arrows pointing into C, from A, B and E, are drawn in accent; the arrows C sends to B and D are not counted. The card reads in-degree 3." width="100%"} In-degree is the number of edges pointing into the node. Only meaningful for directed graphs. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node ID or label. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of incoming edges. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#8f580433 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("C", "B") ) graph.get_in_degree("B") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: "A" has no incoming edges at all: ::: {#40d5d72e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_in_degree("A") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 0 ``` ::: :::
